:::{#cor-deriv-lincom-tp}

#### Derivative of a dot product, transpose-product form

If $\vx$ is constant with respect to $\vb$, then:

$$
\underbrace{\deriv{\vb} (\underbrace{\tp{\vx}}_{1 \times p} \underbrace{\vb}_{p \times 1})}_{p \times 1} =
\underbrace{\vx}_{p \times 1}
$$

:::: notes
This vector derivative formula looks a lot like non-vector calculus,
except that you have to transpose the coefficient:
in scalar calculus $\deriv{x}(cx) = c$,
but here the coefficient $\tp{\vx}$ (a row vector)
becomes $\vx$ (a column vector) in the result.
::::

:::
